mechanism: Chlorthalidone-induced hypokalemia and hyponatremia may increase risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmias; naltrexone may potentiate opioid withdrawal symptoms if used concurrently with opioids; both drugs can affect fluid/electrolyte balance.
action: Monitor electrolytes (potassium, sodium) regularly; assess baseline and periodic ECG if risk factors for QT prolongation exist; ensure adequate hydration and sodium intake; coordinate use if opioid therapy is anticipated.
